# Deep Dives

The twelve chapters of this book take the science-of-deep-learning angle on modern AI: networks as model organisms, phenomena as the object of study, synthetic experiments as the method. There are several **adjacent fields** the main spine deliberately does not cover in depth — not because they are less important, but because each of them is *a discipline in its own right* and could fill a textbook of its own.

This section collects short standalone chapters on those adjacent fields. The framing is **launching points, not summaries**: each entry tries to convey what the field is, what its central questions are, what kind of training someone in that field gets, and where to go next if you want to actually learn it. None of these chapters is a substitute for a real course in the field. They are pointers — but considered, opinionated pointers, written for someone who has finished the main spine and now wants to know what *else* is out there.

If you came here looking for what the main book chose to set aside, you're in the right place.
